newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt starts oil production from Qattara basin.
newsitem.headline: Egypt starts oil production from Qattara basin.

text.p: Agiba Petroleum, a joint venture between Italy's Agip SpA and the Egyptian General Petroleum Corp, has started production from the Qattara Depression in the Western Desert, official sources said on Thursday.
The production, now running at 3,800 barrels a day, is from two fields, Faras in the Ras Qattara concession and the Raml field in the West Abu Gharadiq block, they said.
Agip's Egyptian affiliate, International Egyptian Oil Co (IEOC), shares the concessions with British Gas and the Croatian company INA Naftaplin, the sources added.

Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi inaugurated the fields at a ceremony on Wednesday but by then production had already started, most recently at Raml, where Agiba has just one exploratory well against four production wells in Faras.

Asked if the company planned to increase production from the area, a company executive said it was monitoring production at this stage. "The production looks goods and it fits in well with the concept of developing the Western Desert," he added.
The Qattara Depression, which lies below sea level, is a particularly difficult place to work because of the temperature extremes and the salt-encrusted surface.
